title: Cerebellar examination
stem: Cubicle 24. Mr Man, 66, with hypertension and diabetes, developed sudden unsteadiness, vomiting and slurred speech 3 hours ago. Perform a cerebellar examination and explain your findings.
notes:
Checked against standard neurological examination and ESO/AHA stroke guidance on posterior circulation stroke.

Cerebellar signs (DANISH): Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia (gait, truncal), Nystagmus, Intention tremor and past-pointing, Slurred (scanning) speech, Hypotonia (and pendular reflexes). Also heel–shin, tandem gait, Romberg (positive in sensory or vestibular ataxia, not typically in pure cerebellar disease — a cerebellar patient is unsteady with eyes open too). Signs are ipsilateral to a cerebellar hemisphere lesion; midline (vermis) lesions give truncal ataxia.

Sudden cerebellar signs with vascular risk factors: cerebellar infarct or haemorrhage — emergency CT and CT angiography (MRI DWI is more sensitive for posterior strokes), stroke team (thrombolysis/thrombectomy for basilar occlusion), and neurosurgery for cerebellar haemorrhage over 3 cm or hydrocephalus — the posterior fossa is small and swelling compresses the brainstem.

Your notes list the full cerebellar examination and causes (unilateral: vascular, tumour, MS; bilateral: alcohol, phenytoin, Wernicke's, MS, Miller Fisher, paraneoplastic) — this matches.

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Speech, eyes, arms (finger–nose, rapid alternating), legs (heel–shin), gait (if safe).

Head.r: Horizontal nystagmus, fast phase to the right, worse looking right.

Arms.r: Right: intention tremor and past-pointing. Left normal.

Legs.r: Right heel wavers down the shin.
Leans to the right; needs support.

Legs.t: Make him walk heel-to-toe across the room alone
Legs.r: He can't sit unsupported — walking him risks a fall. Test gait only when safe.

Other.t: Limb power and sensation; other cranial nerves
Other.r: Power normal; no facial or sensory loss.

steps.label: Present and plan
steps.hint: Right cerebellar syndrome, sudden onset: stroke pathway, CT/CTA, neurosurgery if haemorrhage.

opts.t: Right cerebellar signs of sudden onset in a vascular patient: right cerebellar stroke until proven otherwise
opts.mark: Localises to the right cerebellum and suspects stroke

opts.t: Stroke team; urgent CT head and CT angiogram (basilar/vertebral)
If haemorrhage > 3 cm or hydrocephalus: neurosurgery; monitor GCS closely

opts.r: Limb ataxia and dysarthria are central signs.
